newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Under fire Israeli PM names 'Mr Clean' top lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Under fire Israeli PM names 'Mr Clean' top lawyer.

text.p: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu, whose previous choice of attorney-general reeked of back-room politics and ensnarled him in a criminal inquiry, nominated a replacement hailed on Monday as "Mr Clean".

Elyakim Rubinstein, a 49-year-old Jerusalem court judge, has the unique distinction of having served as cabinet secretary in governments of both Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and the late Yitzhak Rabin's left-centre Labour party.

He made history in Madrid in 1991 as chief negotiator at Israel's first peace talks with Jordan and the Palestinians. Extending a hand to his comrades under the glare of television lights, Rubinstein addressed them as "my friends".
"I believe he will add a lot of honour and a lot of accountability to the judicial system in Israel," Netanyahu said in announcing the appointment late on Sunday.
Many across the political spectrum agreed, contrasting with the convulsions caused by his previous appointment of Jerusalem lawyer and Likud insider Roni Bar-On.

Opposition leader Shimon Peres of Labour, asked what he could say about Rubinstein, told Israel Radio: "Only good things. He is an extraordinarily intelligent guy." Cabinet approval is expected on Wednesday.

Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office, caught in a swirl of debate over his having got the job more for his Likud loyalty than legal acumen. Then a television report gave rise to charges the appointment was not just poor judgment but also criminal.

On Sunday, police launched an inquiry into the Channel One television report that Bar-On's appointment was part of a deal with Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, a political kingmaker on trial for corruption since 1993.

It said Deri, an ultra-Orthodox Jew and ex-cabinet minister, demanded Bar-On's appointment in return for his party's support for Netanyahu's accord with the PLO on an Israeli pullback from the West Bank town of Hebron.

The television said as part of the deal, Bar-On promised Deri a plea-bargain that would have enabled him to get on with his political career. The cabinet later approved the Hebron deal with Shas's support.
Bar-On, Deri and Netanyahu all denied the charges. Netanyahu, in office only seven months, demanded an inquiry.
A Tel Aviv-born religious Jew known for his quick wit and extraordinary memory, Rubinstein was hailed by Israeli newspapers on Monday as a wonder boy and man of consensus.
"With Rubinstein there will be no legal deals under the table -- everything will be according to the law and its spirit," wrote correspondent Tova Tsimuki in the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth.

From 1977-81 Rubinstein was a key adviser to foreign ministers Moshe Dayan and Yitzhak Shamir. He took part in peace talks with Egypt, including at Camp David. In 1985-86 he served as deputy chief of mission to Israel's Washington embassy.

Appointed cabinet secretary in Likud Prime Minister Shamir's government in November 1986, Rubinstein remained on the job under Labour's Rabin from July 1992 until May 1994. Later he became a Jerusalem district court judge.
In an interview with the Times of London published on Monday, Netanyahu took aim at Channel One television, vowing to privatise the state-owned station "the sooner the better".
"I think anybody can say what they want, provided they can back up their statements. But the important thing is to give greater choice by having a multiplicity of channels," he said.
